runs.text: A student explains a topic from memory, then gets feedback against a saved checklist.
A web app for focused recall and practice
Introduce Explain It Back as a college software engineering project. The demo follows one study session, from source material to a second explanation.
Each attempt uses the same saved checklist, so the student can focus on what changed.
Paste notes or upload a text PDF.
Save topic titles and key points.
Walk through the learning cycle. Topic extraction happens when material is added. The app reuses those stored key points for each attempt.
Start with the notes the student wants to learn.
Paste a chapter or class notes into the study material field.
Use a readable, text-based PDF. Scanned or handwritten pages are not supported.

On the Upload page, name the material if useful, choose an existing folder or create one, then paste text or choose a PDF. Wait for topic generation to finish. Long material may take longer to process.
The checklist stays hidden until submission.
Topic title and a short summary.
No key points to copy while explaining.
Type up to 5,000 characters, or use optional browser speech input. Submit when ready.
Open a topic from its card. Point out that only the title and summary appear before submission. Type a brief explanation from memory; voice input is optional and depends on browser support.
The results page also shows evidence quotes and detected incorrect statements.

Explain the division of work: Gemini classifies checklist points and provides evidence. Backend code applies the importance weights and calculates the final percentage. The results page also reports incorrect statements separately.
Missed and partial ideas get keyword cues and flashcards. Flip a card to check the answer.
Re-explain the topic, then use the progress chart to compare current mastery, best score, and past attempts.
Show Study missed points, review one keyword set or flashcard, and select Re-explain topic. Then open the progress chart and explain what the latest score and best score represent.
Sends study material or an explanation to the project API.
Extracts topics and key points, then checks explanations against the saved checklist.
Validates Gemini responses with Zod, stores checklists in SQLite, and calculates scores in code.
The API key stays on the server. The checklist stays hidden until the student submits.

The browser sends material or an explanation to the Express API. The backend calls Gemini. After Gemini returns, the server validates the response with Zod, saves checklist data in SQLite, and calculates the score in code. The API key stays on the server.
Weighted score calculation and status mapping.
Zod validation for topic and grading responses.
Grading output with missing, duplicate, or unknown IDs.
Text extraction, chunking, and text-based PDF parsing.
SQLite persistence, speech input, and LLM timeouts.

Inputs: pasted text or readable text-based PDFs. Speech input is optional and browser-dependent. Best suited to theory-heavy material. Scanned notes need OCR; math and code explanations can be harder to grade.

This closing slide gives the professor a concise view of the test coverage and current boundaries. Mention that the project handles pasted notes and readable text-based PDFs, with optional browser speech. It is aimed at theory-heavy topics; scanned notes need OCR, while math and code explanations can be harder to grade. The video link opens the demonstration folder.
